title.quote: Trained Without My Consent: Detecting Code Inclusion In Language Models Trained on Code
title.value: Trained Without My Consent: Detecting Code Inclusion In Language Models Trained on Code

extractions.description: The paper proposes TraWiC, a model-agnostic, interpretable membership-inference-based approach to detect whether code from a project was included in an LLM's training dataset. It extracts syntactic and semantic identifiers from scripts, masks them, queries LLMs (SantaCoder, Llama-2 7B, Mistral 7B) under a Fill-In-the-Middle objective, compares outputs by exact match or Levenshtein edit distance, and trains classifiers (random forest, XGBoost, SVM) on hit features. Results are compared against code clone detectors NiCad and JPlag.

type.quote: In our experiments, we observe that TraWiC is capable of detecting 83.87% of codes that were used to train an LLM.
type.justification: The paper runs experiments with LLMs, fine-tuning, classifiers and reports performance metrics.
